subject: IRT after CAT - Solving non-random missing issue

messages.author: f5ec732b3eb1ad38
messages.subject: IRT after CAT - Solving non-random missing issue
parts:
Hello Dr. Chalmers, 

Thank you for designing the mirt package and creating space for questions. I have inherited data from a CAT. Unfortunately, the items' difficulty scores were previously estimated using a data set in which responses were largely artificial, not based strongly on real person responses. So I would like to improve the item difficulty estimates.

The CAT has been administered and now, but only ~5% of items from the item bank are administered per person. Being adaptive, the test does not administer items randomly, and the amount of non-random missing data is generating poor person ability estimates (fscores() show poor correlation with an external measure of ability I have access to). 

I am new to IRT, and searching the literature on this post-CAT situation (essentially an issue of non-random missingness, I believe) has turned up little guidance so far. ChatGPT has not been much help yet either! Is there any way to pre-load "known" difficulty estimates in order to improve person ability estimates and subsequent item difficulty estimates? I have seen if using the 'pars' option to enter the pre-existing difficulty scores as d values might help, but am not seeing that change the final estimates, and I think I am misinterpreting the purpose of the pars option.

Any direction, even to other resources, would be greatly appreciated!

Sincerely, Peter

messages.author: 71bfb5f1e96782a8
messages.subject: Re: IRT after CAT - Solving non-random missing issue
parts:
hi,

if you don't see any change after adapting d through the pars argument, you're maybe missing to fix the d's by setting est = FALSE. a more reasonable alternative to fixing d parameters to specific values would be to use priors.

best, felix
